utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. For the record, all the accused are present. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. Absent amongst the Defence teams, I notice Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Krgovic, Mr. Lazarevic, and Mr. Haynes. All right. Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I hope you've had a good rest. Mr. Vanderpuye will finish his cross-examination. Then we will see if there is a re-examination, which I think there will be, and we can call it a day as far as you are concerned. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good morning you to, Mr. Markovic. I wanted to pick up a little bit from where we left off on Friday. I had shown you a videotape that had been slowed down, and I understand that that was actually shown to you in a smaller resolution than could have been shown, and so I would like show you it again in order to assist you in identifying the object depicted on the bottom right-hand side of the screen. Again, this is a video clip wherein the action that you see on the tape immediately precedes a conversation wherein Mr. Borovcanin says: "Oficir, or" and there is a response and he directs that person to stop traffic. So I want to focus your attention on that, and if I could play the once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just focus you on the right-hand bottom corner of the screen. Are you able to recognise that object as a microphone commonly attached to a mobile radio?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to make that recognition, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can make out on this video, which has a very bad resolution, I must repeat, is the radio device behind the wind screen of the automobile; and the object in the lower right corner, I really can't recognise because the resolution is very poor. And I really cannot see any difference as compared to last time I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I show you 65 ter 3892, please. I'm sorry, do we -- is it not in -- 3892. Yeah. Okay. Thank you very much. And if we could go to page 2 of this document. All right. If we are able to below up the picture a little bit, that would be helpful. Just for the record, this is a photograph of Mr. Borovcanin taken from an article from Nin magazine, and it's dated 11 April 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, from this photograph, sir, and if you want we can zoom in a little bit, can you make out what radio that is Mr. Borovcanin is holding in his hand, his right hand?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person in the photograph is holding a handheld radio station based on the outlines of the antenna, although this is a black and white photograph with a poor resolution. So based on the outlines of the antenna, I suppose that this is a device operating at a wavelength of 0.7 metres, or to put it simply, that operates on the frequency between 460 and 500 megahertz. But it could also be a device operating on the wavelength of 2 metres. It is difficult to tell based on the outlines of the antenna.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you're not able to determine based just upon the antenna what device this is, whether it's 0.7 metres or 2 metres device. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said before that based on the outlines of the antenna, I suppose that this is a device operating on the wavelength of 0.7 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've not seen this particular photograph before, have you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that same goes for the photographs I showed you on Friday wherein Mr. Borovcanin had two radios on him -- or you were able to determine at least two antennas, those photographs?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have said as much last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could show 65 ter 3889, please. Just for the record, on the previous exhibit, that photograph, it is the Prosecution's position it depicts Mr. Borovcanin at Potocari, and if we get it up a little bit just after this, I can show you that it also depicts Vujadin Popovic in the photograph, and I just want to make the record clear with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, this particular device, I hope, is a better photograph of the GM300, which is what I showed you on Friday. Do you recognise it as such?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, but we didn't see this, the Popovic on the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am going to put it back up on the screen. I just want to finish this question, and then I'll put it back up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this particular device as the GM300?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the GP 300. This is the GM300, and this looks like a compact unit, but I must explain that it is composed of two parts. The upper part is the radio device, and the lower part is the speaker, which comes with the radio device. There is a third component, and that is the microphone combination with a spiral cable, which is compatible with the GP 300 and the GM300.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And those particular microphones are typically used with these types of devices; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they come with this type of device. This is the basic combination for this device, but this microphone combination is compatible with the GM300 and the GP 300. It can be used with the handheld radio device as well as with this device shown here, which can be mounted into vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, for my friend, if I could have 3892 back in e-court. If we could just blow that up a little bit, maybe a little bit bigger. If you look just behind Mr. Borovcanin's right hand, slightly to the left, there's a gentleman there you can see with a dark hair and a mustache.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is it identification by the counsel or by the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, it's simply -- it's simply -- it's simply our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a submission you are making.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct. And the reason why I want to be clear is so that my colleague has a chance to obviously see it fully. It is not a definitive identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course not. Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps we can be told what this question has to do with this witness's expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. We still have to hear the question properly, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The issue was only raised to accommodate my friend. The question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- in relation to the radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Provided you don't tell the witness who that person according to you is, we can safely proceed with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, sir. I'd asked you some questions concerning the responsibility of a communications unit to set up communications with respect to combat operations. Let me show you 65 ter 3893.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't believe we have a translation in e-court, but I have one that we can put up on the ELMO, which I think will assist the parties. I don't know if we can show the translation on the ELMO. Can we do that? Okay, great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a document that is directed to the command of the special police brigade. It is dated 11 July 1995. And what it purports to do is to provide that command with a copy of a coded map that is entitled "Grmec," a code book which is entitled "Krivaja 95," and a work plan for Krivaja 95 together with the identification signals, etc., signed by Nedo Jovicic. If you look at the second page of this document, you can see the call signs that are attributed to various units. In addition to that, you can see a call signs attributed to the MUP, together with frequencies, frequency table, and a signals table, you can see at the lower part of the page. Now, you're familiar with these types of documents, are you not?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first have to say that the first document I saw - not this one, the previous one - is a handwritten document as far as I know, although at the time I wasn't there. But based on my experience, no officer would have drafted such a document, especially in this type of handwriting. We can see from the heading that it's a Drina Corps, and it's obviously the command of the corps. I don't believe that any officer would agree to send out a document of that type, but it wasn't there at the time. I must repeat, therefore, I don't know what the practice was. And about this document, I must say that this wasn't made by a telecommunications officer if it is such a document as you say it is. I can see call signs here and unclear frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "unclear frequencies," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be specific, in the fourth column, the first frequency is 250. Is it -- 250 watt, or possibly it's 1250, or possibly this one is the item number. And I would have to know what this 250 refers to, kilohertz or megahertz, and I cannot recognise any device. From the moment I joined the VRS, I haven't met a device operating on this frequency of 250 megahertz. And in the next column, it says 352. This is, again, a frequency and not a channel because the heading reads "frequency," and I don't know that frequency. And then this is followed by a grid of numbers and letters. This is probably for encoding, but this certainly was not made by a telecommunications officer. But I must add that I wasn't present at the time; therefore, I don't know what the practice was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, what about frequency 171? Do you recognise that frequency? Item number 9, where it says MUP, OBLAK, 9.171. Do you recognise that frequency?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say what I see at the moment. I see 9.171. Whether this figure 9 is part of the frequency or the item number, I don't know. And if it's just 171, there is no unit of measure. It could be kilohertz or megahertz. That's an open question. The heading reads only "Freq." And then in this particular field, it has a 9.71, and to the right it's 20.403, but this is not a common plan of work of the type I know. This may be an innovation, but I don't know the practice at the time. And again, there is no unit of measure, megahertz or kilohertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you don't recognise that 1 through 22 actually constitute the number of frequencies you can see in that plan, right? You don't see that 1 down through 11 is numbered is sequence, and 12 down through 22 is numbered in sequence? You don't recognise that in your experience and expertise as a communications officer?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to make conjectures, and this is not a standard kind of work as it was used in the JNA and later in the VRS. But I repeat, I wasn't present at that time, so I don't know what kind of plans of work they used. The standard type is a printed template, which is then filled in, and if you make one by hand, then it will have -- well, it will have to be of the same dimensions and of the same shape. This is not a standard layout. And these are the frequencies. For the frequencies, no unit of measure is given, so I don't want to guess what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. For the record, it is the Prosecution's position that the preceding document, which is page 1 of this document, was prepared by Nedo Jovicic who the Prosecution believes was Mr. Borovcanin's driver on the 13th of July, 1995. Just page back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the document in your possession an original one or a copy of one?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will determine whether or not we have the original. I believe we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether the stamp, Drina Corps command stamp, which appears on page 2, the -- is stamped on your -- at page 2, not on page 1. And the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe it is stamped only on page 2. That's correct. And this was part -- and it's a series -- it's within a range of documents that also bear similar stamps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So if you could check it later on and tell me whether you have an original or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I most certainly will, Your Honour. If I could just have a look at page 1, the translation for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, before you do so. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am very sorry to interrupt, but I am not quite sure I understood the position of the Prosecution. Is the position of the Prosecution that this document comes from the command of the Drina Corps, has been drafted by a member of the special police?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just look --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just look at the translation, I'll be happy to answer the question. I don't have a copy in front of me. I do now. I can see that it's received by Nedo Jovicic, and that's our position, is as depicted in the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear that it's been received by that person, what the Prosecutor has just said. He said it was a document prepared by that person, and that's why I was not understanding what he -- was being said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if you -- thank you, Madam Fauveau. If you look at page 9, lines 6 and -- 5 to 7, it says precisely what Ms. Fauveau has just stated; namely, that you are put on record as saying that it's your position that the preceding document, which is page 1 of this document, is prepared by Nedo Jovicic who the Prosecution believes was Mr. Borovcanin's driver on the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct. I said that. But I said it looking at an untranslated version of the document. It was a misstatement that I wish to clarify, which is why I asked to see the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think it's clear enough now, no? Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, my understanding is that the purpose of stating a position is to state it for the witness so the witness can then respond in some intelligible way to a position that relates to the witness's knowledge. That's not what actually's going on now. Now what's going on is a series of submissions about the nature of a document. I would also have many submissions on that, but I don't think it's appropriate to do it, nor do I think it's appropriate for my learned friends to be doing so, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're partly right, but it's also a statement made for your information, as well, so -- because you still have a chance of a redirect. So at that point in time, I don't criticize Mr. -- let's proceed, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to this document that was received by Nedo Jovicic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is the Prosecution's position that he was Mr. Borovcanin's driver on 13 July, 1995 --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In your experience as a communications officer, it is indeed likely, is it not, that Mr. Borovcanin was provided with precisely the information that's contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think that crosses the line. I think we're now into speculation and outside of the witness's expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your comment, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think this witness is fully familiar with the procedures with respect to relaying a communications plan to a commander in respect of the deployment of a combat operations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Stop, stop, stop, because it's now that you are overstepping, perhaps. Witness, I will repeat to you the question: "In your experience as a communications officer, isn't it likely, isn't it, that Mr. Borovcanin was provided with precisely the information that's contained in this document?" If based on your experience you are in a position to give an answer and an answer based either on certainty or on a basis of probability, balance of probability, then yes, please go ahead. If it was a question you need to speculate, you don't know, then please don't answer the question at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this particular case, may I just see the Serbian version of the document, please, because I'm just looking at the English translation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's looking at ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of what I can see, all I can do is comment and say that if this is indeed a document, then there are several things lacking here. First of all, the degree of secrecy and confidently particularly when it comes to documents sent out from the corps, you have state secrets, strictly confidential, confidential, and so on. And that's something that I don't see on this document, especially if it's a document that's strictly confidential. Now, the second point here is this: All it says, from the corps command, but it doesn't say who handed the document over, which, for a strictly confidential document of this kind, is compulsory. Now, whether it could have reached the command or not, I really can't say. However, I would never send the commander a document like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to know whether the witness is talking of the first page or of the second page; in other words, what we see on e-court now or whether it's the other document with the stamp, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you understand Mr. President's question, sir? If you could answer it.

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just a handwritten document. That's the one I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that's the one you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and I've already said what I think about it. That is to say, I don't know whether this could have been sent out or not. I can't say with any certainty. So I just repeated what I saw, my visual observations. If this is the document that was indeed sent out, then I told you what the floors were, what was lacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that, Mr. Markovic. If I could take you just briefly to a different area. I showed you a photograph on Friday with respect to a vehicle, that it's the Prosecution's position Mr. Borovcanin was riding in on 13 July 1995, up and down the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. What I would like to do is follow that up and show you another photograph of the same antenna.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I believe that is 65 ter 3859. If I -- on the left-hand side of the screen, maybe we could make that a little bit bigger. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to identify this type of antenna?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the contours, the outlines, and as I say the resolution is a bad one on this photograph, all I can say is that this is a magnetic antenna which is placed on vehicles; that is to say, one that's used for this type of device, the 0.7- and 2-metre frequency type or wavelength type.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That type of antenna isn't normally or -- hooked up to a portable radio device, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I can't see it very well, and I can't see the dimensions of the antenna from a 2-dimensional picture, but every frequency range in both wavelengths had different lengths of antenna; and here, you can't see the length of the antenna at all. But this type of antenna can go with a radio device, but usually there are standard ones which are fixed to the vehicle with the frequency range for that particular device.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But this particular antenna that you see here is not a type of antenna that's hooked up to a Motorola GP 300 or a Motorola 0 -- or OP 030, right? It's hooked up to different type of radio device?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's not placed on the GP 300 or OP 030. It is hooked up to a radio device which is built into a vehicle or the call stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you 65 ter 3891. This is a page from the Motorola GM300 service manual. All right. What I want to show you is -- well, as you can see for yourself, it says accessories, and I apologise. I don't have a B/C/S translation of this document. But specifically what I'm referring to are the types of antennas that are listed here for this particular device, and you can see VHF antennas from 146 to 150.8 megahertz. It says quarter-wave roof mount, and the same for another antenna from 158 to 162 megahertz, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but this may be helpful. Apparently, the translation to the witness of line 2 of page 15 actually gave GP 300. Of course, that's -- that's not what counsel said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But we could see the model number on the screen in any case. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, it's just that it's not on the actual document shown to the witness, so I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. But we're talking of GM300.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What this document depicts are the specifications -- well, no, I'm sorry. They depict the accessories for the GM300. That's the mobile radio, and you can see various antennas that can be used with this device. Among them are several roof mount antennas. Now, the photograph a that I just showed you, that would be consistent with a roof mount antenna such as the ones described in this particular document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what you've just shown me, the accessories for the GM300, these are models of the various antennae and the type of antennas, depending on the manufacture and the different names given. And on the right we have the technical data, which I am able to comment on. So the first one here is 146 to 150.8 megahertz, and it's characteristic is 1/4, if that's what it says. I think so. It's the wave roof mount, mounted on the roof. So the 1/4 is a wavelength over 4, and it is the exact wavelength, and the wavelength is calculated on the basis of the frequency spectrum or the operator being posed. In this case, it is 146 to 150.8 megahertz. And so on the basis of that, once you obtain the wavelength/4, you have the length of the antenna for that range. The first from the -- the fourth from the top, where it says 146 to 172 megahertz, for example, you have three decibels, which means that the length -- it's not the length of the antenna that is calculated there. It's just the amplification of the antenna with -- at the receptor --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, what I want to know is --

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- or the gain roof mount. So we have different frequency ranges and different possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, you can see from this document that there is an antenna roof mount available for every frequency to which the GM300 can transmit and receive. What I want to know from you is, based upon your knowledge and experience with these types of things, in particular with antennas and radio communications type devices, whether or not you have -- you can tell us whether or not these types of antennas are consistent with the appearance -- appearance-wise with the ones that you -- the one you just saw in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you in answer to your question is this: First of all, the document that we see here are types of antennas for those particular ranges, and from the technical point of view, I can say that the one I saw, the outlines I saw, I can say it is a magnetic antenna which is mounted on the roof of a vehicle, and I can also tell you that it is used in one of these frequency ranges. On the basis of the 2-dimensional picture, we can't see the length of the antenna itself; and therefore, I cannot confirm which frequency range this specific antenna that I saw on the photograph is used for.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You know that the GM300 does transmit and receive within the frequency range of 146 to 172 megahertz. We went over that on Friday, and according to this work plan in the document I showed you before that was received by Nedo Jovicic, that the MUP was assigned a frequency of 171. That would fall within that frequency band, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can tell you, if it is indeed 171 megahertz as you claim, is that it would come within that frequency band. However, on the basis of the document I was shown, I have to repeat that I cannot recognise this because it's the not the standard type of document that was used. And at the time I wasn't there. I wasn't present, so I don't know what they used. But 171 megahertz does fall within the 2-metres wavelength or 146 to 170 megahertz or 174, actually, megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, in your report you made certain assessments as to the quality -- I'm sorry, as to the quality of the communications that could be achieved between the points that you've indicated. And what you described was the quality between Sandici and Kravica warehouse of 5 over 5, or 5 by 5; and then you described the quality of the sound between Sandici and Hrncici as 2/1. Now, with respect to those particular descriptions, those are essentially subjective measures of sound quality, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That is correct. They are subjective measures of sound quality, and they have to be subjective because I used the device on that occasion, so it's what I heard and necessarily subjective. If it's subjective, then it doesn't hold water.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There are ways, of course, of measuring the sound quality through instrumentation or objective means, aren't there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Of course, there are. You can measure sound quality through instrumentation and objective means. But on the basis of the procedure we used in the armed forces, it was the subjective type that was used, a subjective assessment, because the operator using the radio device is the person who received and sent out information. So he is the person who assessed the quality of the communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So with respect to this particular analysis that you did, you didn't use anything like an S metre or a power metre or signalling tester or any of those kinds of technical devices, transmitter testers, et cetera, right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. But let me just mention that during the testing I conducted, I had very limited resources and equipment because all these devices that you mentioned would require much more time, far more money, for the purchase of such equipment or for renting it out, and these are resources which I simply did not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, one resource you did have was your partner's field notes, which you indicated on Friday that you hadn't completely reviewed in respect of preparing this report, right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat what I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want you to answer the question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, I've already answered that question. That's why I said I'll repeat it. We compiled the report together, and of course, he used his field notes to compile that report, and that's how the report was written.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But you didn't review his field notes, right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not 100 per cent. Just the portion that was -- that I was interested in, the geographic location where the communication testing was performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You could have, for example, requested or obtained the specifications of the devices that you tested. You didn't do that, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This exact question was asked on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember yourself asking the question, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly asking the question. I do remember that the witness said he hadn't relied on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But that's a different question of whether or not he tried to obtain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to your specific assignment in performing the tests - and correct me if I'm wrong - did you get any specific instructions from the Defence as to which specific locations to test from?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on my conversation with the Defence and the assignment given me - not by them, I mean, but my superiors in the Ministry of the Interior - I was told point 1 and point 2. I knew where that was, but not the exact geographic coordinates; but roughly speaking, I and my colleague in the communications department set these coordinates in that location, Sandici "livida," and the Kravica warehouse in this particular case. And in both those cases, they were along the road several metres away, one way or another, but there are -- with the GPS, we had exact location points.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how did you come to measure your locations at Nova Kasaba, at Konjevic Polje and at Hrncici in particular if you weren't instructed to do that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went along the road, along the communication line from Kravica towards Zvornik, moving towards Zvornik; and then I chose some of those locations randomly and performed the testing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So all of the locations besides Kravica and Sandici, you arrived at in your report for testing purposes completely randomly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Hrncici too. We didn't know that location, but with our tests and checking out the radio communication, we were able to establish where the lines had been interrupted, and the others were at random, the other two. We tested radio communication along the road from a vehicle, which was not possible, and then at one point I decided to stop the vehicle and test the communication there outside the vehicle, and it was a main road. So we tested it there outside the vehicle, and communication there was not possible. So those are the GPS points that were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is there any particular reason why you didn't test for any communication possibilities from Kravica in the direction of Bratunac randomly?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no particular reason. We just tested that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, for your indulgence. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Gosnell, redirect if you still wish to have one. Incidentally, today's sitting will be as follows. We'll have a first session until 10.30; then a second session from 11 to 12.30; then we are going to stop until 3.00; and then we start at 3.00 and finish at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll do my best to be done by 10.30, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to make sure it wasn't taken as a suggestion to take up until 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll do my best to avoid that result, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Markovic. You were asked a series of questions about Annex 1 of your report, which is a representation of the terrain between Sandici and Kravica warehouse and beyond. Now, first of all I would like to ask you, does the accuracy or inaccuracy of this graph have any bearing on the field test that you conducted between Kravica warehouse and Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it does, yes. The soil profile does correspond, but there was optical visibility. And as you can see on the soil profile in Annex 1, that would be it. And, of course, we have here the altitudes, but I'd also like to say that the soil profile was a little longer -- a longer soil profile was taken because the profile allows for a soil profile of over 2 kilometres. And in this case, it is 1.2 kilometres where optical visibility does exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand there may have been a portion of your answer that was not translated, so let me ask the question in a slightly different way. Did you rely on this graph in conducting your field test?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked exclusively with physical testing in the field, from point 1 to point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So does that -- does that mean that you're telling us and the Court that you did not rely on this graph in conducting that field test?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We relied directly on the physical testing and radio communication between those two points. This is just to show -- the graph is just to show that there was visibility, optical visibility between the two points.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And did that fact, the fact that you were not relying on this graph and that you were conducting a field test, did that have an impact on how much time, money, resources that you spent in preparing this particular annex?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that our resources were quite limited. We received no funds for the testing. We relied exclusively on the physical testing of the radio communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we call up 4D607, please, page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to notify the Court and my colleagues that we do have the originals of the document that was received by Nedo Jovicic in Court for inspection if anybody wants to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've testified that the horizontal -- in concerning the horizontal axis of this graph, that the left-hand point is Sandici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, can you just point out or explain for us where Kravica warehouse is on the horizontal axis of this graph?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be precise, but in the text it says 1.2 kilometres, and I will try to mark that distance on the graph. It would be approximately around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And does that accurately reflect the altitude of Kravica warehouse? I'm sorry. There's a translation error. I understood that the word "altitude" was translated as "distance," so perhaps I could just repeat the question. Does this line graph accurately indicate the altitude of Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this, we can see the altitude; however, it is very difficult to measure it based on this. In any case, the altitude would be around here. This was also shown by our GPS measurements. The distance in terms of altitude between Kravica and Sandici existed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The difference, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could you please mark the red dot in the middle of the graph with a 1.

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And sir, you've described that that represents the location in respect of the horizontal graph -- or the horizontal axis, the location of Kravica warehouse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is 1.2 kilometres. However, as I've said, I cannot be precise using this pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you please sign this document and put today's date.

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And could this be saved, please. All right. We are done with this page. Can we now move to page 15 of, again, the same document, 4D607.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've testified that a field test is more accurate than a HerTZ Mapper projection, and you've also testified that you based your results in your report on your field tests and not on the HerTZ Mapper projection. What I'd like you to explain to the Court, if you can, is, in general terms, if a researcher is going to conduct a field test, why would they bother with a HerTZ Mapper projection?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct we relied exclusively on the physical measurements of communication between the points. As I said, we wanted to put it in graphic terms in order to explain what it looks like in the field. In the crime police administration, in the department I work for, this tool is used so that we would be able to know what there is in the field, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When you say "to know what there is in the field," what do you mean by that in general terms?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms, we merely look at what we can expect to find in the field. We try to assess where we will have good communication and where the points are where that needs to be checked. However, we can never fully rely on this software to indicate that. We always have to check irrespective of the colour indicated on the mapper.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, the Prosecutor asked you during his cross-examination why you didn't repeat your field tests on subsequent days. Do you remember those series of questions?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you a few questions about that. You testified that the conditions on the day of your test were between 8 and 9 out of 10 on a scale of ideal atmospheric conditions. Did that play a role in any way in deciding whether or not subsequent tests on subsequent days were necessary in order to validate your results?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to state again that we were limited by the weather conditions. Given the fact that the conditions were between 8 and 9 on that day, it means that the weather conditions could only have been worse than that, making radio communication at that point more difficult. In any case, in order to check that, we have to test in different weather conditions in the field. We were limited in terms of time, and given that we were working under good conditions, although they were not ideal, we did not find it necessary to double-check that the next day. And I also have to say that the weather conditions did not change the subsequent -- the next day, so nothing would have changed due do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we zoom in on the document that's on the screen right now a little bit. All right. That's great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you describe during your testimony that you established contact with your test partner at Sandici meadow as you drove towards Konjevic Polje every 20 or 30 seconds. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, based on your best recollection, how many times would you say that you established contact with your partner as you drove towards Hrncici when you lost contact?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say precisely. I think between 10 and 15 times, approximately every 20 to 30 seconds. Those were the intervals at which we checked radio communication. All I can say that we check communication frequently before arriving at the point in Hrncici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was there any pattern that you were observing as you were checking these 10 to 15 times? Was there an observable pattern in terms of the quality of your contact with your test partner?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no pattern. It was not a linear pattern.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me put it a different way. Were you finding that you were gradually losing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye. One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's a leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was planning on putting it in a non-leading fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hear it in its entirety, and then we decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you find, if the course of these 10 to 15 occasions, that you were gradually -- that the quality was gradually decreasing, or rather, did you find that when you reached Hrncici there was a sudden drop-off from full quality contact to no contact?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's still leading. If my colleague wants to know, he can simply ask the witness what he observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. I mean, you did add something to it, but it -- you only made it worse, I think. So you could ask him what he found, I mean, but I know it will not get you anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When you did lose contact at Hrncici, was it a surprise to you based upon your previous 10 to 15 contacts with your colleague?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Communication ceased all of a sudden at a certain point in the course of those 20- to 30-second intervals. All of a sudden, there was simply no communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, did you observe any degradation between the first point of contact, the first time that you contacted your colleague, and let's say the penultimate time that you contacted your colleague before Hrncici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you answer. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's the same objection. It is still leading. My colleague can simply ask the witness what he observed in relation to his testing between those two points. I don't know why he won't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I think any degradation is wide open. The witness can answer any way that he wants. It doesn't lead him to an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Go ahead. We are not underestimating your objection, but we think it's on the margin here. So please proceed with your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand it fully. All I can say is that there were changes; but as I said, there was no linear or clear pattern because of the lie of land. At a certain point when we were checking communication, we arrived at the conclusion that at that point there was no communication. It was interrupted at a certain point. Then we turned back, and we used shorter intervals to check radio communication, and at a certain point we managed to re-establish communication again. Then we turned the vehicle again and lost communication again. We stopped at that point, and then I tried to establish communication outside of the vehicle on the other side of the road, and this is where I established that the radio communication was 2/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So do I understand from what you're saying that you turned around in order to try to test or make contact with your colleague again in order to specifically and precisely determine the exact spot where you would lose contact with him?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did that twice in order to pinpoint the location at which there is no radio communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And once you stepped out of the vehicle, as you've testified, in order to test in the open air whether you could contact your colleague, how long would you say you stood outside of the car trying to make that contact?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that I spent up to five minutes outside of the vehicle, maybe a few more minutes than that because I was also taking GPS coordinates and noting them down. In the course of that period, we tried to check radio communication on several occasions in order to establish what the audibility was. Moving up and down, I covered the distance of between 5 and 10 metres to all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So are you saying you moved around in order to see whether that would change your ability to speak with your colleague at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is standard procedure. We change our position in all directions trying to establish the best possible communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that answer. The Prosecutor asked you a number of questions about your alleged failure to give a detailed description of -- well, the moving about that you've just described in order to try to establish contact with your colleague. And during your testimony in response to one of your -- one of my learned friend's questions, you gave the following answer. You said: "And in the end, when operating at such distances, and when using such radio devices, the Motorola GP300 or some other kind of device, well, the results would not have been significantly different." Can you please explain to the Court why you said that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that because irrespective of the type of radio device you use that works based on the similar characteristics, would not have resulted in any significant changes in terms of radio communication because the characteristics are the same or similar. The only possible difference could be if strong-output power devices were used. However, all handheld devices, depending on the make, have their maximum output of up to 5 watts, or better yet, around 5 watts. Some makes may have the power of 4 or 6, but that doesn't change anything. During tactical movements out in the field, what is characteristic for such devices is the maximum range of 2 to 5 kilometres depending on the terrain, or rather, the altitude to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd like to come back --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to come back to the process of driving towards Konjevic Polje from Sandici --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just for my learned friend, this is relevant to something that was asked on cross-examination, but I'm going to reveal that at the end of a series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As you -- after you immediately left Sandici meadow, do you remember what the quality was of your contact with your colleague on the very first test? The very first time that you tried to establish contact with him, how good was the quality?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that communication is first established at close range in order to test the devices. But if we are talking about the first occasion on which communication was established from the vehicle driving towards Sandici, that was at 5.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And in general terms, there is no need to be absolutely precise, but in general terms can you estimate for us how far in metres you were from Sandici meadow when you made that first contact and reached a result of 5/5?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be precise because it is downhill from Sandici, and I think it's between 150 and 200 metres that the distance is over there. In any case, I think it was around 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me then just cut to the chase for what I really want to get to. If you can recall and to the best of your recollection, when you were 400 metres from Sandici meadow, what was the quality of your contact with your colleague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I object to the question for two reasons, Your Honour. If my colleague is eliciting this witness's recollection of precisely what he did as concerns these tests, it is clear in the record that this witness took notes with which we were not been provided, not had the opportunity to look at those notes to verify whether or not his recollection now that he's testifying here is accurate. We've had no ability to challenge that. And so to the extent that we haven't been provided with that information, I would argue that it's improper for my colleague to elicit that information because those notes exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Your comment, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, actually, to be quite honest with the Court, I don't know if there's any note that concerns the subject matter of my question, and I don't believe that that's been established yet. So the notion that there may be a note that hasn't been handed over, I don't think that's been established. I can't tell you positively that no such note exists, to be quite frank with the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I'm referring to is this witness's testimony with respect to his taking of field notes with -- concerning his -- concerning the tests that he conducted. And he's indicated that he did in fact take notes both on cross-examination and now also on redirect examination, and I think to the extent that those notes exist as he's testified to and that we've never been provided with a copy of those notes or had an opportunity to review them that it places at an unfair disadvantage with respect to his now-present recollections about what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Witness, if you were to answer the question put to you by Mr. Gosnell, on what would you base it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would base my response on my own observations. I cannot recall what the precise distance was in terms of metres. All I can recall is that after the Sandici meadow, immediately close by, there is a bend in the road. There were changes in terms of radio communication there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think we can safely proceed from here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you this question. You were shown a videotape by the Prosecutor, on which there was audio, and you were asked to comment on the quality of that audio, to give a rating of what was presented to you as a transmission through a radio. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, the question I am -- wish to put to you is, was the sound that you heard on that audio consistent with what you would have observed at a position 400 metres from Sandici meadow when contacting your colleague? Are the two -- would the two types of quality be consistent in your mind?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not completely. At close range from Sandici, I had 100 per cent audibility. What I could hear on the recording is what I received through the amplification in my headset, and that is what I could subjectively hear at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying you're not sure whether that would or would not be consistent with the transmission from Sandici?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain. I cannot say that with any degree of certainty. It was subjective, what I could hear in my headset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have the break now, resuming at 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice that the witness is not present and Mr. Josse standing. Is there a problem, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, a double apology. The first apology is for interrupting the re-examination. Secondly, frankly, I should have realised that the issue I am about to raise might be an issue because we did have advanced notice of it. But I am aware now that there is a two-and-a-half-hour break today, and I have some concerns for my client where he's going to spend that two and a half hours. I wrote about an hour or so ago to the court officer expressing my concerns. Bearing in mind that that break is in just over an hour's time, I felt this was my opportunity and only opportunity to raise it with the Trial Chamber, but it's simply not acceptable in my submission for him to the spend the two and a half hours in an extremely small holding room immediately behind where I sit. He, in fact, has proposed what I will call a sort of compromise, which is that some doors be left open and a guard stationed more or less where I am at the moment so that he could at least walk around the corridor behind where I am at the moment. But whether that's acceptable, of course, is not a matter, I understand, for the Trial Chamber nor indeed for the person of the guards who are presently in Court at the moment. But, Your Honour, two and a half hours in that room with the door shut with no air at all is simply not acceptable, I submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and I would understand that your colleagues would associate themselves with this. Yes, let's do it this way, and it needs to be resolved very quickly. If a modus vivendi is found which is acceptable to the accused, then we'll do that. If not, the accused are to be transported at the end of the sitting to the detention unit and returned as soon as practicable before we start the -- re-start the sitting at 3.00. If it's not possible to bring them back before 3.00, we'll even start later. But the important thing is that they are not allowed to stay in these small cells that we have here for two and a half hours. So, Madam Registrar, you are to communicate our instructions to the Registrar forthwith, and if Mr. Josse's suggestion is acceptable to the Registrar in security --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I can see some dissension from some of the defendants in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I wasn't looking at Mr. Borovcanin. Yes, Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would sooner stop breathing for an hour and a half than being brought back to the detention unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Borovcanin seems to prefer to stay here. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he prefers to stay here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think some of the rooms on the other side may a be a little bit bigger.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Josse is perfectly right. I just want to correct the transcript. I was talking about Mr. Miletic, my own client, because the transcript is not very clear on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I took you to be doing precisely that. Yes, Mr. Gvero.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED GVERO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please accept my apologies, but I must say that the rooms where Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Miletic are dwelling are different. They have a toilet and water and a hallway, but my room is extremely small. Thank you for attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I may ask, are there more rooms like the one in which Miletic and Borovcanin are that -- in which Gvero could be accommodated? No. How many rooms? Just seven here, or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but this courtroom was, I think, even planned to take 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's the small rooms immediately behind where I am sitting. The two accused who are detained there, my client and General Pandurevic, and the rooms there are small. There are some other rooms amongst that suite of rooms if I can grandly call it that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps one could inquire if Mr. Borovcanin is prepared to swap with Mr. Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, precisely so. That's why I'm on my feet. I am informed that my client does -- is willing to swap with Mr. Gvero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I see Mr. Borovcanin nodding, so that could provide a solution, if that is acceptable, of course, with the security people. The problem is that after 12.30 we will not be available to -- we are unapproachable because we have a plenary immediately after, so a solution has to be found now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I repeat my apology. I am sure it can be found. I also invite the supervisor of these guards to consider the compromise that I suggested to them earlier and to the Trial Chamber; namely, that a couple of doors be kept open with proper and adequate supervision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But obviously, they have to refer to their superiors. I mean, they can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I really do understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. We are proceeding with our investigations on this and will come back to you. In any case, you are also to communicate that Mr. Borovcanin is prepared to swap rooms with Mr. Gvero, if that is okay with the security people, of course. Thank you. For the record, Mr. Mitchell for the Prosecution is also present today, now. He wasn't before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Hello, Mr. Markovic.

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just one last question on what I was asking you about just before the break, namely, the audio that you heard that was played to you. Just to be clear with you, the Prosecution position in this case is that that audio that you heard was at a point 400 metres from Sandici meadow along the road. Now, my question for you is, can you exclude the possibility, based your observations, that that transmission was from Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the recording, I cannot say where the vehicle was at that moment, but I can say that it must have been very close, that there must have been optical visibility given the good quality of the communication. But I cannot draw any other conclusion from the video recording. I can make the subjective conclusion based on what I heard in my headset that the quality of communication between the two radio devices was very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I am not sure where my colleague got the impression that it was the Prosecution's position that that particular audio was 400 metres from Sandici. I don't think that's in the record, and I don't think that I stated that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That is based on our consultation of the road book and what appears to be a relevant still from the piece of video that was shown which corresponds to the still that is in the road book, which indicates it is 400 metres from Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll look into that because I think I'm looking at the still now, and the caption is that it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. If we need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- over a thousand metres from Sandici meadow but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we need to return to this, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- we'll look at that another time. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can just resolve this ambiguity right now with another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you make the same -- would you give the same answer if I were to tell you that rather than 400 metres from Sandici meadow, you were 12 -- the audiotape was 1.200 metres from Sandici meadow? Could you exclude the possibility that that transmission was from Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To establish that precisely, you would have to conduct measurements in the field; that is clear. But based on everything I have said so far, the quality of communication that I heard from the audio recording must have -- would indicate toward a short distance. And if I understood you well, the 1.200 metres from Sandici toward Konjevic Polje would not -- would not affect the communication significantly. The communication would still be understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Markovic, you were asked a number of questions based on the video still of the corner of an object. You were shown that video still on Friday and again today in a larger format. And the Prosecution suggested to you that this was a handheld microphone that was attached to a car-mounted radio. Now, sir, to your knowledge, can handheld microphones be attached to handheld portable radio devices?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The microphone combination is compatible with most devices manufactured by Motorola, so they can be attached to both handheld radio devices as well as car-mounted radios.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd now like to play a short video clip and see whether you can recognise anything on this video clip; or rather, I will then direct your attention to specific items and see if you can recognise them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you require sound or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Perhaps we could play this two more times, and then freeze it at the end of the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, first of all I'd like to direct your attention to the left of centre of the screen at the bottom. Is there anything that you can recognise there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this video still that I have on the screen in front of me, I can recognise the outlines of an antenna, probably for a wavelength of 2 metres. The image is somewhat blurred, but I can recognise the outlines of an antenna.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And just to the right of the centre of the screen, do you recognise an oval-shaped dark object, and can you offer an opinion as to what that might be?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, I repeat the image is a little blurred, but I can make out the outlines of a microphone that can be used -- or rather, connected to a handheld radio device. I can only make out the outlines. I cannot see the details because the image is blurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we see the video played one more time, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you see any car-mounted radios in this video such as a GM300 or an FT2400 Yaesu?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can only see the outlines of a handheld radio device, and I can draw the conclusions that it operates on the wavelength of 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, sir, you remember you were shown a video clip surrounding --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We can now take down the video clip on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You were shown by the Prosecutor a video clip surrounding the video clip that you saw earlier today, and do you remember that you saw an object on the dashboard?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw a handheld radio device on the dashboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, how many did you see?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Markovic. Now, I want to ask you some questions about car-mounted radios that were discussed at length during your cross-examination. Now, did you test the GM300 or the FT2400 Yaesu car-mounted radio as part of your field testing?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't test those devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were you ever asked by the Defence to test those devices?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we never received such requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. In the absence of such tests, can you state with any specificity the precise spot where communication would be lost as between a car-mounted radio and a handheld radio as you move from Sandici towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JOVO MARKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were ongoing communication, let's say that a handheld radio is emitting on a certain frequency, and a car-mounted radio with a roof-mounted antenna because otherwise it can't operate. It could operate within the car, but that is not practical. In such a case, communication would not differ significantly from the point of view of reception. If the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps I could just pinpoint my question because maybe it was very poorly phrased. My question was, if you had the transmitting device - being the handheld radio - at Sandici and the receiving device is a car-mounted radio, and then -- now, here is my question: Can you state with any specificity at what point reception would be lost as you moved up the road towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question calls for speculation as concerns the reception of a radio signal. This witness has testified that its dependent upon the sensitivity of the receiving device; and so this calls for speculation to the extent that the witness hasn't tested the device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I am precisely attempting to determine the line between what he can comment upon and what would be speculation. That's precisely what I am attempting to do with my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't consider it calling for speculation. Actually, it's calling for a professional opinion. So go ahead and answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, the results wouldn't change greatly, the results that we obtained in the field, because it depends on the strength of the transmitter, the handheld radio; whereas reception depends on the sensitivity of the antenna. But due to the configuration of the land, there wouldn't be any significant changes in the field. Of course, in order to bear that out you would have to conduct physical testing of that premise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I raise the objection again. My colleague here hasn't put to the witness what specific radio he's talking about; and to the extent that they differ, depending on their characteristics, depending on their specifications, the answer is not responsive, and it is -- it is fundamentally speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I strongly disagree. The parameters of these radios are generally similar. The witness said that he didn't field test it. That wasn't basis for my question, so I think his opinion is perfectly legitimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you offer your own comments on what you've just heard? Would it make a difference to you if you are specifically referred to a particular radio rather than another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say that the transmitting radio devices and those mounted in vehicles are completely compatible with respect to frequency depending on the type and manufacturer. They can be compatible; and what I said, my assertions require field testing, as well, but what I think on the basis of my experience is that if we use a radio -- a handheld radio device and a radio device in a car, mounted in a car, this would not change the results significantly, the results that we arrived at by testing. But what I want to say is that on the basis of my experience, the results would probably be truthful ones, but they would have to be tested by other measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Incidentally, sir, in your experience have you ever seen cars driving around or vehicles of any type with antennae on the roof without a working car-mounted radio?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If my colleague wants to put that to the witness, I would ask for him to state whether or not that is the position of the Defence in this case; otherwise, I don't think it has any relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, we don't have to take a position in this case because we're the Defence. It's up to the Prosecution to state its position. We don't need to take any position whatsoever. So it's perfectly fair to me to explore alternatives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's proceed. Let's proceed with the -- with your answer, witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand that the question may not have been properly translated to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's try and get this over and done with, please. What hasn't been properly translated, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The word "working" apparently was not translated to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I will repeat the question. "In your experience have you ever seen cars driving around or vehicles of any type with antennae on the roof without a working car-mounted radio?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, based on my experience I have not seen anything like that happening, nor is there any reason for anything like that to happen. Let me just make it clearer: The connectors that are mounted to the antennas of handheld radio devices are different to the car ones. So the antennas on the roof are used for vehicles and radios in vehicles, and if there's no radio device, I don't see why there should be an antenna on the roof just as an obstacle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, again, perhaps the question wasn't -- at least a portion of the question wasn't translated to you, and it may be rather obvious, but I'll pose the question anyway. Does the presence of a rooftop antenna necessarily mean that there is a working car-mounted radio inside?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's been asked and answered; and moreover, this is practically a rhetorical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
